描述_EN: by the beginning of the 7th century large quantities of silver pieces with exotic shapes and styles were imported along the silk road from iran and central asia to china. a series of rings inside one another were attached to one half to ensure that the central saucer remained upright even when the incense burner was rolled around. silver objects were not as highly coveted in china as in other ancient civilizations such as the roman or the parthian, but they became important luxury items for emperors and high-ranking officials during the tang dynasty (ad 618-907). during the same period chinese craftsmen also acquired new manufacturing techniques from central asian silversmiths who had settled in chinese urban centres beginning in the mid 7th century. this censer consists of two hemispherical shells which are locked together by a bayonet fitting to form a sphere. this device was invented by the chinese in about the 2nd century and probably derived from the armillary spheres used by astronomers.
描述_ZN: 到7世纪初，大量具有异国风格的银器沿着丝绸之路从伊朗和中亚进口到中国。 一系列的环状物彼此相连，以确保中央的碟子即使在香炉翻滚的时候也能保持直立。 银器在中国并不像其他文明古国如罗马或帕提亚那样受到高度关注，但在唐朝（公元618-907年），它们成为皇帝和高级官员的重要奢侈品。 在同一时期，中国的工匠们也从7世纪中叶开始在中国城市中心定居的中亚银匠那里获得了新的制造技术。 这个香炉由两个半球形的外壳组成，通过一个卡口配件锁在一起，形成一个球体。 这个装置是由中国人在大约2世纪发明的，可能来自天文学家使用的浑天仪。
